text:
Connor McDavid has a point in all 20 of Edmonton's games, and the shape of it is pure McDavid: 38 assists, 11 goals, 22 power-play points, nearly 24 minutes a night. He goes to Toronto, his hometown, carrying the league's loudest Hart Trophy buzz and a little unfinished business. The Leafs beat the Oilers 7-2 on October 24, and in a reporter's preview he put it plainly: "They fed us our lunch last time."

Some of this will come back to earth. He has 11 goals on 7.8 expected, shooting 20% against 16% last season, and the Oilers have scored 20.3 more goals than their chances deserve with him on the ice. Our talent range puts his true scoring rate around 4.5 points per 60; he's running at 6.2.

But the engine is real. Edmonton owns 61% of the expected goals at five on five with him out there. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him carrying the puck in on 68% of his entries last season, and Evolving-Hockey rated him the most valuable forward in the league. The streak is the headline. The play driving underneath it is the part that lasts.
headline: Twenty games, twenty with a point
